newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil state votes to impeach bond scandal suspect.
newsitem.headline: Brazil state votes to impeach bond scandal suspect.

text.p: The governor of the Brazilian state of Santa Catarina on Monday faced impeachment for his alleged role in a multimillion dollar municipal bond scandal, an official at the state legislative assembly said.
"The governor's impeachment was passed and they are currently voting on the impeachment of the vice governor," a spokeswoman for the Workers Party (PT) told Reuters.

Although the state assembly voted by 29-11 to start the impeachment process against State Gov. Paulo Afonso Vieira, the Supreme Court earlier ruled he would be able to remain in his job for 180 days to prepare his defense.

Vieira, together with leading politicians including former Sao Paulo Mayor and presidential hopeful Paulo Maluf, was accused of participating in a scheme in which brokers allegedly skimmed millions off state and municipal bond issues.
As voting continued over whether to impeach several others, including Vice Gov. Jose Augusto Huelse, scuffles broke out among congressmen inside the assembly, the PT spokeswoman said.
Members of Vieira's Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB) sharply protested the voting procedure and the session was temporarily suspended.
A small group of demonstrators in favor of Vieira broke a glass pane outside the assembly, the spokeswoman added.

The bond scandal, through which more than $400 million may have been deposited in secret bank accounts in Paraguay and the Caribbean, has echoes of the corruption probe that toppled former president Fernando Collor in 1992.

Senators heading a parliamentary investigation say states and cities sold their debt at below market prices to friendly brokerages, who in turn passed the securities on for a considerable profit to others involved in the scheme.

Celso Pitta, mayor of the country's largest city Sao Paulo, has been questioned on suspicion that he was involved in the scheme during his tenure as the city's finance secretary. Pitta has denied doing anything wrong.
